subject: Renewal: bucket smoothing + performance rebate proposal
messages:

Subject: Renewal: bucket smoothing + performance rebate proposal

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for the renewal conversation last week. Per our note, I put together two compact options that aim to: 1) smooth EdgePoint’s mid-contract growth (so you don’t get hit by sudden uplift invoices), and 2) keep unit economics predictable while giving you upside if we meet the agreed performance targets.

Option A — Smoothing + Conditional Rebate
- Commit: keep current annual commit, allow a temporary 30% burst pool for 60 days to cover onboarding spikes.
- Invoicing: any burst consumed is billed pro-rata monthly but can be reallocated into the next month’s bucket.
- Rebate: if average 95th percentile latency <= 350ms and model availability >= 99.8% during the quarter, EdgePoint receives a 7% rebate on token spend for that quarter (applied as credit to next invoice).

Option B — Tiered Uplift with Blended Rate
- Commit: incremental growth tiers with blended rate caps (first 20% growth at 8% uplift, next 20% at 5%).
- Invoicing: true-up at quarter end; partial pro-rate for mid-quarter additions.
- No performance rebate, but deeper guaranteed pricing at higher tiers.

Attached: EdgePoint_Renewal_Worksheet.xlsx — I filled in example consumption curves and the resulting monthly invoices under each option. DraftAmendment_v2.pdf shows legal-friendly language for the temporary burst and rebate clause.

Questions for you: which outcome is more important — cost smoothing (Option A) or predictable tiered pricing at scale (Option B)? Also, do you need the temporary burst to be active immediately after signing, or can we schedule it for your planned migration window in January?

If helpful, I can also map these to a PO timeline for Procurement. Happy to jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the worksheet.

Thanks,
Dylan

Dylan —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the worksheet — very helpful. A couple quick clarifying items before we loop legal/procurement: 

1) For Option A, can you show an example month where we consume the full 30% burst and how the credit flows if the performance rebate is met? We want to make sure there’s no double-billing risk during the reallocation.
2) For the rebate: is the latency SLO evaluated against p95 or p99? You quoted p95 but our internal SREs typically ask for p99 — curious what you recommend operationally.
3) Procurement asks whether the temporary burst requires a change to our EIP (contract identifier) or if it can be handled as an amendment. Also confirm your standard PO lead time for an amendment sign-off (we aim to put POs in the queue 3 weeks before effective date).

We’re leaning toward cost smoothing (Option A) because we have a Q1 onboarding spike, but we need clarity on the pXX metric and the billing flow. Can we set a call for Friday 10–10:30 PT? Procurement will join.

Best,
Samantha Lee

Samantha — thanks, and great questions. Answers below and I attached a worked example (same workbook, second tab).

1) Burst consumption example (Option A) - Scenario: monthly baseline 1.0M token units, burst cap 30% => up to 1.3M tokens month. If you consume full 1.3M in Month X:
  - Billing: Month X invoice shows 1.3M consumption at standard unit rate.
  - Reallocation: if you elect reallocation within 30 days, we credit up to the committed bucket of the following month (we do not retroactively reduce Month X’s invoice; the credit appears on the next invoice).
  - Rebate interplay: rebate is calculated on net billed spend for the quarter after credits are applied. So there’s no double-billing — credits are reconciled before rebate calculation.

2) Metric for rebate — p95 vs p99 - Operational recommendation: p95 is a better signal for general latency behavior; p99 catches long-tail noisy infra events. We can structure the rebate to use p95 as the primary threshold and a p99 guardrail (e.g., if p99 breaches > 1% of requests, rebate reduces by half). That way you get meaningful upside while we protect against tail risk.

3) Contracting/PO timeline - The temporary burst can be added via a simple amendment (no EIP rewrite). DraftAmendment_v2.pdf is structured as an amendment with an effective date window. Standard PO lead time: 2–3 weeks for amendments in our experience. If you need it faster, Marissa and I can coordinate an approval path and Ben can pre-clear billing codes to accelerate procurement.

I’ve summarized the ask/next steps below so Procurement has everything for the PO queue:
- Decision: Option A (smoothing + burst + rebate) preferred by EdgePoint
- Effective date requested: 2027-01-03 (migration window)
- PO target submission: 2026-12-15
- Follow-up call: Friday 2026-11-13 10:00–10:30 PT (please confirm)

If that works, I’ll have Marissa start the signature routing and Ben prepare the invoice example for the PO.

Thanks,
Dylan
